mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in real personal consumption expenditures, proxied by a decline in GDPC1 over two consecutive quarters, reduces aggregate demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where GDPC1 declines for two straight quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer and business confidence, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over four consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of episodes where INDPRO declines for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (core inflation) above 3% signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of months where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS rising >0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months) boosts consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive months with PAYEMS >0.5% MoM growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over the same month signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both fall month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of months where both HOUST and GDPC1 decline MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% combined with a fall in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a synchronized labor and supply shock, which increases recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% AND INDPRO < 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during months where UNRATE > 5% and INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average.
